//stt: whisper-cpp:       whisper.cpp's whisper-server, on this machine or another. Needs url.
openai-compatible: POST {url}/audio/transcriptions. Needs url and model.
Groq:   { provider: openai-compatible, url: https://api.groq.com/openai/v1, model: whisper-large-v3 }
OpenAI: { provider: openai-compatible, url: https://api.openai.com/v1, model: whisper-1 }
sarvam:            POST {url}/speech-to-text. Indian languages and code-mixed speech.
Sarvam: { provider: sarvam, model: saaras:v3, language: unknown }
url and model default; language is BCP-47 (hi-IN, en-IN, ta-IN) or unknown to auto-detect.
Either provider may carry a credential, sent as Bearer: apiKey, apiKeyEnv, or apiKeyFile.
apiKeyFile is a path relative to this file; setup writes those with mode 0600.
//server: publicBaseUrl is OPTIONAL: where this server answers from somewhere that is not
this machine. `tama expose` writes it for you. Set it by hand if you put a domain
or a proxy in front, so `tama-server connect` prints an address a client can reach
instead of 127.0.0.1. An origin only - no path, no query. http is fine for a tunnel
or a LAN address; Meta's webhook still requires https.
//server-oauth: OPTIONAL, and only meaningful with a public hostname. Adding this block turns on
OAuth 2.1 so a connector dialled from someone else's servers - ChatGPT, a Claude
custom connector - can authenticate. Without it there are no OAuth endpoints and
the local accountless path is unchanged.
readView/writeView are view names applied to every OAuth grant; absent means the
owner decides per connection on the consent screen. extraRedirects adds a callback
for a client that is neither vendor. cimdOrigins are the only origins whose client
metadata documents will ever be fetched.
//whatsapp: OPTIONAL. Register a dedicated number with Meta's WhatsApp Cloud API and expose
https://your-host/webhooks/whatsapp. Voice notes capture; text messages use Ask.
allowedFrom is the explicit vault access list: country code + number, digits only.
Keep the access token, Meta app secret, and your random webhook verify token outside this file.
//ask: OPTIONAL. Delete this whole block and capture still works with no account and no key;
POST /ask just returns 501. Adding it turns on question answering over your notes.
anthropic:         model e.g. claude-sonnet-5. Key here or in $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
openai-compatible: one adapter covering Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio, vLLM, OpenAI,
Groq, OpenRouter, Together. Needs baseUrl. Local needs no key.
Ollama: { provider: openai-compatible, baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1, model: qwen2.5:7b }
OpenRouter: { provider: openai-compatible, baseUrl: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1, model: openrouter/free, apiKeyEnv: OPENROUTER_API_KEY }
//ask.limits: maxChunks: excerpts retrieved per answer, 1-25 (default 8, clamped above 25).
Each is capped near 400 characters, so this is the input bill.
maxTokens:  output cap per answer (default 2048). A gateway prices a request
by this before generating, so omitting it inherits the model's own
maximum and can be refused as unaffordable.
//ask.pin: Notes put in front of the model on EVERY question, chosen by path instead of
found by score. Retrieval can only return what a question's words match, so a
file describing how your vault is organised is unfindable by it: no question
shares vocabulary with it, and scoring it would spend a maxChunks slot.
conventions: durable structure. Which note is the source of truth for a
subject, which are generated and disposable, what the folders
mean. This one overrides 'prefer the newer note', so a daily
scratch file stops being treated as authority on what is current.
state:       what is live right now. Preferred over older notes for anything
Both are read as untrusted note text, exactly like an excerpt, and neither can
change the model's instructions. 8 notes maximum, 32KB each, 64KB in total,
and anything skipped or cut is logged once. Omit the whole block to pin
nothing, which is how this worked before pinning existed.
